title: Dispatch tokens: format, draft and verify, signed by the operator's root (decision 1, option 5)
description: First build task of the identity design the operator ratified on 2026-10-21. Tokens only; no wiring.
acceptance_criteria: A new tool, .harness/bin/token.py (another name only if it collides; justify), with at least: draft, which any agent may run and which emits an UNSIGNED token set for one epic, one token per (agent_name, task_id, role, issued_at, expiry, nonce), and prints the exact ssh-keygen -Y sign command the operator runs, mirroring warrant.py draft; and verify, which checks a presented token against the enrolled root (.harness/trust/root.pub), its expiry, and that the presented (agent, task, role) match.

The signature is an SSH signature by the operator's root key with a namespace distinct from warrants'. Never an HMAC or any shared secret: under D-17 every agent could read it. A test asserts that no code path in the module can sign, the same shape as warrant.py's.
Grain: one signed file per epic carrying that epic's tokens (ruling 2026-10-21). A token is valid only if its epic file's signature verifies against the enrolled root.

Falsifier tests from the design, using a throwaway root in a temporary directory: a valid token is accepted; a tampered agent_name is refused; an expired token is refused; a token for (worker-a, T-999, worker) presented as worker-b is refused; a set signed by a key that is not the enrolled root is refused. State whether nonces are single-use and test whichever you choose.
No wiring into blackboard.py or lock.py (that is T-454) and no change to any existing behavior. Do not edit CLAUDE.md. The suite passes via goal_mode. Hand off to verifier.

notes.note: plan: new tool .harness/bin/dispatch_token.py (renamed from token.py -- collides with stdlib token module, breaks tokenize import when .harness/bin is on sys.path, verified in scratchpad). draft/verify verbs, SSH signature by operator root in namespace harness-dispatch-token, grain=one signed file per epic, no wiring. Test file .harness/tests/test_dispatch_token.py mirrors test_warrant.py shape.

HANDOFF -> verifier: Built .harness/bin/dispatch_token.py (draft/verify) + .harness/tests/test_dispatch_token.py, no wiring, mirroring warrant.py's shape per the task.

NAME: token.py collides with stdlib `token` (imported transitively by `tokenize`, which `inspect`/`unittest` paths touch). Measured directly: placing a stub token.py on sys.path ahead of the stdlib (as .harness/bin is, in every test file that does sys.path.insert(0, str(BIN_DIR))) makes `import tokenize` raise ImportError: cannot import name 'EXACT_TOKEN_TYPES' from 'token'. Used dispatch_token.py instead; no such collision (python3 -c "import sys,tokenize" after inserting a stub token.py on sys.path reproduces the break -- repro left out of the tree, scratchpad only).

Design followed: fields (agent_name, task_id, role, issued_at, expiry, nonce); grain = one signed file per epic (dispatch_tokens/DT-NNN.json + .sig); signature is an SSH signature by the OPERATOR's root key (reuses warrant.py's enrolled trust/root.pub -- one operator root for both warrants and dispatch tokens, per the 2026-10-21 ruling's own words), namespace "harness-dispatch-token", distinct from both warrant.NAMESPACE ("harness-warrant") and attest.NAMESPACE ("harness-act") -- test_dispatch_token.py::NamespaceIsolation pins both the distinctness and that a warrant-namespace signature does not verify a token set. No HMAC anywhere; verify() only calls ssh-keygen -Y verify.

No-signing-path test copied from warrant.py's shape: TheModuleCannotSign (grep for '"-Y", "sign"' absent from source + per-callable inspect.getsource scan), same as TheHarnessCannotSign in test_warrant.py.

Five falsifiers from the acceptance criteria, each its own test in class Falsifiers: valid token accepted; tampered agent_name refused (TAMPERED, field-compare against the canonical signed token by nonce); expired token refused (per-token TTL override used to force expiry in-test); token for (worker-a, T-999, worker) presented as worker-b refused (IDENTITY MISMATCH, via claim_agent/claim_task/claim_role vs the canonical token's own fields); set signed by a non-enrolled key refused (ssh-keygen -Y verify fails against the anchored root).

Nonces: NOT single-use in this module -- stated in the module docstring (search "NOT SINGLE-USE") and in operator-rulings language terms, not hidden. verify() is a stateless check over a signed file on disk with no consumption-tracking state; T-446 explicitly excludes wiring into blackboard.py/lock.py (that's T-454), which is the only place a "seen nonces" store would naturally live. test_dispatch_token.py::NoncesAreNotSingleUseHere::test_a_valid_token_verifies_twice pins the current behaviour (same genuine, unexpired token verifies twice) so a future change is deliberate, not an accidental regression.

Epic grain pinned: EpicGrain::test_one_signature_covers_every_token_for_the_epic (3 tokens, 1 signature, all verify) and ::test_tampering_one_token_in_the_file_invalidates_the_whole_signed_set (editing one token's field breaks verification for the whole file, via warrant-style file-bytes signing).

No wiring: NoWiring::test_blackboard_and_lock_do_not_import_dispatch_token parses blackboard.py and lock.py with ast and asserts dispatch_token is not imported by either. No existing file's behavior changed; only two new files were created, plus this handoff/artifact note on T-446.json via blackboard.py (no hand-edits).

REJECTED (verifier harness-verifier, T-447 replay of T-446).

REPLAYED, PASSED: python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_dispatch_token.py -q -> 19 passed in 2.64s. python3 .harness/bin/goal_mode.py run --cmd "python3 -m pytest .harness/tests -q" -> GOAL REACHED on iteration 1/3 (118.06s). Static read of dispatch_token.py confirms: no "-Y", "sign" call anywhere in the module; _verify_file_signature always builds allowed_signers from w.trust_dir(root)/root.pub (the enrolled anchor) and additionally compares the signer fingerprint against w.check_anchor(root) -- it never reads a key or fingerprint from the token-set payload itself in the SHIPPED code. Independent adversary probe (own script, throwaway temp root, agent-generated ed25519 key, not the producer's "evil"/"mallory" fixtures): signing a drafted token set with a freshly generated non-root key is refused ("SIGNATURE DOES NOT VERIFY"); embedding a fake "trusted_signer_pubkey" field in the payload JSON and signing with that key is also refused by the shipped code, because the field is simply never read.

FAILED CRITERION (T-447, bullet 3: "verify against any key the file names... Each mutant must make at least one test fail"). Built the mutant in a throwaway copy of .harness/bin (never the live tree): changed _verify_file_signature to source allowed_signers from a "trusted_signer_pubkey" field inside the payload JSON when present (falling back to trust/root.pub otherwise), and removed the subsequent anchor-fingerprint comparison that is the module's only other defense against that change. Ran the FULL unmodified test_dispatch_token.py (19 tests, path-patched to the throwaway bin only) against this mutant: 19 passed, 0 failed. Confirmed separately that the mutant is a live, exploitable break and not a no-op: drafted a token set naming an attacker-controlled agent/task, embedded that attacker's own pubkey as "trusted_signer_pubkey", signed with the attacker's own key (never the operator root), and verify_token_set() returned success, reporting the attacker's own key fingerprint as the signer -- i.e. the module's own stated invariant ("the signing key must be THE anchored key, or nothing verifies") can be silently defeated by a future edit, and none of the 19 shipped tests would catch it, because none of them constructs a payload that names its own trusted key. This is exactly the attack class T-447 bullet 3 and T-432's option-5 ratification (D-17: never trust a key the token/file itself names) were written to pin down with a regression test, and T-446 ships no such test.

Mutants 1 and 2 of T-447 bullet 3 WERE caught as required: skipping the expiry check (`expired = False`) failed Falsifiers::test_an_expired_token_is_refused; skipping the identity-match check (`if False:` around the claim_agent/claim_task/claim_role comparison) failed Falsifiers::test_a_token_for_worker_a_presented_as_worker_b_is_refused. Only the "trusts a key the file names" class has no regression pin.

TODO for the worker before re-handoff: add a Falsifiers (or EpicGrain-adjacent) test that signs a token set with a non-root key while the payload additionally claims/embeds that same key as trusted, and asserts verify_token_set/verify still raises TrustError -- i.e. pin that the signing-key source is ALWAYS trust/root.pub, never anything inside the payload, independent of what the payload claims. No source-code change needed today (the shipped module already does the right thing); this is a missing regression test, not a shipped vulnerability.

Everything else in T-446's acceptance criteria replays clean: namespace isolation, epic grain (one signature covers N tokens; tampering one invalidates the whole file), no-signing-path (AST + source-substring), no wiring into blackboard.py/lock.py (AST-confirmed), nonces stated and pinned as not single-use, live-store isolation. Sending back for the one missing falsifier rather than failing the whole task outright, since the shipped code itself is sound by inspection and by direct adversarial replay -- only the regression coverage for this one attack class is absent.

CHANGE: added one new test to .harness/tests/test_dispatch_token.py, class Falsifiers:
test_a_payload_that_names_its_own_signer_as_trusted_is_still_refused -- drafts a token set, injects a "trusted_signer_pubkey"/"trusted_signer_fingerprint" field into the on-disk payload naming an attacker's own (non-root) key, signs the whole (now-larger) payload with that same attacker key, and asserts verify_token_set still raises TrustError. Also asserts the exception text does not even mention "trusted_signer", to pin that the refusal comes from the anchor-fingerprint mismatch, not from any code path that looked at the embedded field.

VERIFIED THE TEST IS A REAL REGRESSION PIN, not a tautology: built the exact mutant the verifier described (sourcing allowed_signers from a trusted_signer_pubkey field in the payload when present, falling back to trust/root.pub otherwise, with the anchor-fingerprint comparison removed) in a throwaway copy of .harness/bin under the scratchpad tempdir (never the live tree, never committed). Ran the unmodified test_dispatch_token.py against that mutant copy: the new test failed with "AssertionError: TrustError not raised" -- exactly the failure T-447 bullet 3 requires. (Three other tests in that isolated run failed/errored for unrelated environmental reasons -- NoWiring and TheModuleCannotSign's AST reads and NoPrivateKeyIsEverTracked's git-ls-files call all depend on repo-relative paths/.git that the throwaway copy does not have; they are path/environment artifacts of running outside the real tree, not related to the mutant or to my change, and they are absent when the suite runs in place.)
